title: PaperOS library evaluation rubric

anchors.4: Allow-tier SPDX for the context; LICENSE text and license field agree; no CLA, field-of-use limit or attribution burden beyond a notices file.
anchors.3: Allow tier with friction we carry: field/file disagreement resolving in our favour, a required attribution surface, or MPL-2.0 where we may patch files.
anchors.2: Review tier in a context the policy allows with a waiver (LGPL/GPL in dev or service, AGPL-3.0 in service, BUSL-1.1, ELv2, bespoke SEE LICENSE IN); waiver drafted, ADR written, expiry set.
anchors.1: Review tier with the waiver plausible but unwritten, or open core whose free tier is allow-licensed while the features we want are not.
anchors.0: Block tier or unknown: SSPL-1.0, Commons Clause, JSON, UNLICENSED, missing, or any copyleft in a bundled context. Hard gate licenseTier fails.

caps.note: Single-maintainer projects cap at 2 unless a company or foundation backs them; name the backer with a link.

anchors.4: Release within 90 days; 3+ active maintainers or company/foundation backing; median first response under 14 days; published cadence or roadmap; breaking changes ship codemods or a migration guide.
anchors.3: Release within 180 days; 2+ maintainers; median first response under 30 days; issues triaged even when not fixed.
anchors.2: Release within 12 months; one maintainer or a small team with visible backlog debt; median first response under 90 days.
anchors.1: No release in 12 months but the repo is alive (commits, answered issues), or a healthy fork exists that we would have to follow.
anchors.0: Archived, or 18 months with no commit and no answered issue, or the maintainer announced they are stopping.

criteria.label: Bundle size
criteria.measurement: gzipped size of the imports we actually use, from an esbuild metafile over a fixture entry point; vendor claims are not evidence

anchors.4: Under 10 KB gzipped for the used imports; tree-shakeable (ESM, accurate sideEffects); no runtime CSS-in-JS cost; no polyfill pull-in.
anchors.3: 10-40 KB gzipped; tree-shakes correctly; peer dependencies we already ship.
anchors.2: 40-100 KB gzipped, or tree-shakes only with a plugin/config we must maintain, or it drags in one heavyweight peer we would otherwise not ship.
anchors.1: 100-250 KB gzipped, or lazy-loadable only as one route chunk, or it ships a WASM blob we must host.
anchors.0: Over 250 KB gzipped for the used imports, or unbundleable (CDN-only, no ESM).

anchors.4: Correct roles and ARIA out of the box; full keyboard operation with documented focus order and focus trapping/restore; visible focus not suppressed; nothing hover-only or drag-only (every drag has a keyboard equivalent); respects prefers-reduced-motion and forced-colors; 44 px targets or configurable; published a11y statement or APG conformance; upstream tests with a screen reader.
anchors.3: Correct roles and keyboard operation; one or two named gaps with open upstream issues; focus visible; reduced-motion honoured; drag has a keyboard equivalent even if clumsy.
anchors.2: Keyboard-operable with our wrapper: we supply roles, labels or focus management, and the work is bounded and named in migrationCostHours.
anchors.1: Keyboard operation only by replacing the library's interaction layer, or a core interaction is drag-only / hover-only with no keyboard path, or it sets outline: none globally.
anchors.0: Inaccessible by construction (no accessible tree, no focus model) and upstream says it is out of scope; a UI library at 0 cannot be adopted for a customer-facing surface.

anchors.4: Hand-written types shipped in the package; correct ESM + CJS export map (arethetypeswrong and publint clean); passes under strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess and exactOptionalPropertyTypes; generics and inference work with no any at the boundary; typed errors rather than stringly-typed throws.
anchors.3: Hand-written types, sound at our compiler settings; one or two anys at the edges; export map fine; errors typed but coarse.
anchors.2: @types/* from DefinitelyTyped, current with the runtime version we use, or shipped types with known drift worked around in one place.
anchors.1: Generated or partial types that lie about the runtime, or types that force skipLibCheck or a ts-expect-error, or @types/* lagging a major behind.
anchors.0: No types at all and none on DefinitelyTyped. Hard gate noTypes fails.

anchors.4: Markdown docs or llms.txt / raw-markdown route; typed copy-pasteable examples that compile; small orthogonal API surface; typed errors with actionable messages; stable naming across versions; well known to Claude so a session writes correct code without fetching docs; a Context7 or MCP docs source exists.
anchors.3: Good docs in Markdown or easily fetched HTML; examples mostly typed; moderate surface; Claude knows it but not the current major, so a session must check the changelog.
anchors.2: Docs are a generated API reference or a hard-to-fetch site; examples untyped or JS-only; several ways to do the same thing; one doc fetch needed per non-trivial use.
anchors.1: Docs are a README plus source reading, or the current major renamed things the model remembers by their old names, or the API depends on implicit global state a session will not guess.
anchors.0: No usable docs; the only reference is a Discord, a video course or a paywall.

naRule.description: An n/a criterion is dropped and the remaining weights are rescaled proportionally to 100 (or to 100 - sum(extraWeights) when extras are used). The rescaled weights are recorded on the scorecard as rescaledWeights.

extras.rule: Extras take their weight out of the base six, which rescale proportionally to 100 - sum(extraWeights). Every extra ships 0-4 anchors written out in the ADR, and the same extras with the same weights are applied to every candidate in the comparison. Extras never remove a hard gate.

anchors.4: OpenSSF Scorecard >= 7.0, no open advisory above low, signed releases or build provenance.
anchors.3: Scorecard >= 6.0, no open advisory above moderate, releases from CI.
anchors.2: Scorecard >= 5.0, open moderate advisory with a patched version available.
anchors.1: Scorecard >= 4.0, or an open high advisory with a patched version available.
anchors.0: Scorecard < 4.0, or an open high advisory with no patched version.

anchors.4: publint and arethetypeswrong both clean; correct exports map, ESM + CJS, no dual-package hazard.
anchors.3: Both clean apart from warnings we do not hit.
anchors.2: One tool reports a problem we configure around in our own build.
anchors.1: One tool reports a problem we must patch the package for.
anchors.0: Either tool reports an error class we would have to patch around permanently.

gates.label: License tier
gates.failsWhen: The SPDX expression is outside the allow tier for the candidate's context and no unexpired waiver in ops/licenses/waivers.yaml covers it.
gates.clearedBy: Waiver plus ADR; block tier needs Justin.

gates.label: No TypeScript types
gates.failsWhen: No types ship and none exist on DefinitelyTyped, for a candidate with a JavaScript surface.
gates.clearedBy: ADR exception naming who maintains the .d.ts.

gates.label: Tauri WebView incompatibility
gates.failsWhen: A UI candidate does not work in webkit2gtk (Linux) or WKWebView (macOS/iOS): Chromium-only APIs, unsupported CSS, or a crash in the spike.
gates.clearedBy: A tested fallback path recorded with the spike artefact.

gates.label: Vendor cloud with no self-host path
gates.failsWhen: A hosted vendor with no self-host option and no data export we can run on our own box.

gates.label: Open critical advisory
gates.failsWhen: An open critical advisory exists with no patched version.
gates.clearedBy: A patched release, or a registered pnpm patch entry with an expiry.

gateRule: Gates are evaluated before scoring. Any gate with result 'fail' forces verdict 'reject' regardless of the total; a scorecard whose verdict disagrees is invalid. 'waived' requires an ADR id.

thresholds.note: Registry status adopted; usage note and version pin required.
Allowed behind one module boundary or feature flag, with an ADR reviewDate no more than 90 days out.
Not used; recorded so the next session does not re-litigate it.

evidenceRule.message: Scores of 3 or 4 require a URL or a repo path in evidence; pnpm lib score exits non-zero and names the criterion.

licensePolicy.draftTiersSupersededBy: ops/licenses/policy.yaml — PAP-211 merged, so the fallback below is dead data; removing it is PAP-1013
licensePolicy.onFallback: print 'license policy: draft (PAP-211 unmerged)' and set facts.licensePolicySource = 'draft'

open-core.note: a needed feature behind the paid tier caps license at 1 and needs a Needs Justin card

fields.facts: embedded facts.json or a path to it
fields.gates: { <gateId>: { result: pass | fail | waived, evidence, adr? } }

flags.--facts-only: emit facts without scoring, for PAP-218 pre-scores
flags.--facts-from <dir>: read a spike kit results/summary.json so measured FPS and bundle numbers populate facts

cli.renders: the Markdown Alternatives table an ADR pastes under 'Alternatives rejected'

changeControl: Weights, anchors, gates and thresholds change only through an ADR superseding ADR 0009, approved by Atlas, naming the scorecards to recompute. Adding a domain extra to one comparison is not a rubric change.
